concepts.title: Development Path and Reform Timelines of India, China and Pakistan

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Development Path and Reform Timelines of India, China and Pakistan' refers to.
questions.a: India, China and Pakistan started development around the same time with planning and public sector roles; China began reforms in 1978, Pakistan in 1988 and India in 1991, with China following a state-led command model before market reforms and special economic zones.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Development Path and Reform Timelines of India, China and Pakistan'.
questions.a: Comparing the three neighbours shows how different reform timings and strategies produced different growth outcomes.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Development Path and Reform Timelines of India, China and Pakistan' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Comparative development (source: keec108.txt development path sections)

concepts.title: Human Development and Demographic Indicators Compared

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Human Development and Demographic Indicators Compared' refers to.
questions.a: The three countries are compared on indicators like GDP growth rate, infant mortality rate, maternal mortality rate, literacy rate, life expectancy, population below poverty line and the human development index, with China leading on most health and mortality indicators and Pakistan lagging on literacy and poverty.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Human Development and Demographic Indicators Compared'.
questions.a: China's one child policy lowered population growth, while India and Pakistan show higher population growth rates that dilute per capita gains.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Human Development and Demographic Indicators Compared' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Human development indicators (source: keec108.txt indicator comparison sections)

concepts.title: Conclusions: Sectoral Shares, Employment and Lessons

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Conclusions: Sectoral Shares, Employment and Lessons' refers to.
questions.a: China has the largest share of workforce in industry and the highest GDP growth, India leads in services with strong engineering and IT exports, Pakistan depends more on agriculture and remittances, and the comparative study warns that development requires attention to health, education and balanced sectoral growth.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Conclusions: Sectoral Shares, Employment and Lessons'.
questions.a: The lesson is that policy stability, human development investment and export orientation together decide development success.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Conclusions: Sectoral Shares, Employment and Lessons' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Conclusions of comparison (source: keec108.txt conclusions sections)
